sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Natalie Kittroweff.
sentences.zh: 我是娜塔莉·基特罗夫，来自《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.

sentences.en: The election issue people are most concerned about is the economy.
sentences.zh: 人们最关心的选举议题是经济。

sentences.en: And President Trump knows it.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统深知这一点。

sentences.en: We have the single greatest moment in the history of our country in terms of the economy.
sentences.zh: 就经济而言，我们迎来了国家历史上最伟大的时刻。

sentences.en: As the midterms approach, Trump has been trying to persuade voters that they're wrong to be so frustrated about the cost of living.
sentences.zh: 随着中期选举临近，特朗普一直在试图说服选民，让他们相信自己对生活成本的沮丧是错的。

sentences.en: We're the hottest country anywhere in the world.
sentences.zh: 我们是世界上最火热的国家。

sentences.en: And saying that instead of criticizing him, they should be grateful.
sentences.zh: 并且说他们不仅不应该批评他，还应该心怀感激。

sentences.en: We brought our pricing way down.
sentences.zh: 我们把价格大幅降下来了。

sentences.en: Oil is right now much cheaper.
sentences.zh: 石油现在便宜得多。

sentences.en: We have almost no inflation, by the way, and we've taken in trillions and trillions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们几乎没有通货膨胀，而且我们收了数不尽的真金白银。

sentences.en: We're richer now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在更有钱了。

sentences.en: We're making more money there than we ever, and we have more jobs than ever before.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里赚的钱比以往任何时候都多，我们的工作岗位也比以往任何时候都多。

sentences.en: Remember that?
sentences.zh: 还记得吗？

sentences.en: Today, my colleague, chief economics correspondent Ben Castleman, explains what the latest economic data actually says and why so few voters are buying Trump's story.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事、首席经济记者本·卡斯特尔曼将解释最新经济数据究竟说明了什么，以及为什么几乎没有选民买特朗普的账。

sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I bring you pastries.
sentences.zh: 我给你带点心。

sentences.en: You explain the state of economy to me.
sentences.zh: 你向我解释经济状况。

sentences.en: This is what we do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的分工。

sentences.zh: 麦克风里传出吃点心的声音，再没有比这更好的了。

sentences.en: And nothing sounds better on mic than you explaining the economy.
sentences.zh: 而麦克风里传出你解释经济的声音，也再没有比这更好的了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 边吃点心边讲。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧。

sentences.en: Ben, it is wonderful to have you back.
sentences.zh: 本，很高兴你能回来。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we know, of course, that people always weigh the economy very heavily when they go to the polls.
sentences.zh: 所以我们知道，毫无疑问，人们去投票时总是会把经济权衡得很重。

sentences.en: This year is no exception.
sentences.zh: 今年也不例外。

sentences.en: We just got this new batch of economic reports that I understand are our last big temperature check before the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 我们刚刚拿到这批新的经济报告，据我了解，这是我们在中期选举前最后一次大规模的体温检测。

sentences.en: So we want you to help us decode this moment.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望你帮我们解读这个时刻。

sentences.en: What is the state of the economy heading into the midterms?
sentences.zh: 迈向中期选举之际，经济状况究竟如何？

sentences.en: So, as you alluded to, right, we just got this big batch of data, this kind of our last snapshot of the state of the economy.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才暗示的，对吧，我们刚刚拿到这批庞大的数据，这可以说是我们对经济现状的最后一次快照。

sentences.en: And we got this sort of whole list of reports.
sentences.zh: 我们拿到了一整串报告。

sentences.en: We got retail sales data.
sentences.zh: 我们有了零售销售数据。

sentences.en: We got claims for unemployment insurance.
sentences.zh: 我们有了失业保险申请数据。

sentences.en: We got industrial production.
sentences.zh: 我们有了工业生产数据。

sentences.en: And we got a boatload of data about inflation.
sentences.zh: 我们还有一大堆关于通货膨胀的数据。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're data rich right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们现在数据非常充足。

sentences.en: We are data rich.
sentences.zh: 我们的确数据充足。

sentences.en: And the story that it tells is nuanced, but the sort of basic takeaway is that there are a lot of real sources of strength in the economy right now.
sentences.zh: 它所讲述的故事是有细微差别的，但基本的结论是，目前经济中存在许多真正的力量源泉。

sentences.en: There's a lot that Republicans on the trail right now can point to and say it's going pretty well.
sentences.zh: 竞选途中的共和党人现在有很多可以指出的亮点，并借此说明情况相当不错。

sentences.en: But there's this big glaring thing that is wrong, and that is affordability.
sentences.zh: 但有一个显眼的大问题出错了，那就是负担能力。

sentences.en: And that, of course, is the issue that matters most to a lot of voters.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是对许多选民来说最重要的问题。

sentences.en: And it's kind of this big blaring klaxon that is going off in the economy right now.
sentences.zh: 它就像是当前经济中拉响的巨大警报器。

sentences.en: And how do you think about affordability when you look at this data?
sentences.zh: 当你看到这些数据时，你是如何看待负担能力的？

sentences.en: How do you measure it as this big flashing warning sign?
sentences.zh: 你如何将它衡量为这个闪烁的巨大警告信号？

sentences.en: So there are really three ways of thinking about affordability here.
sentences.zh: 这里实际上有三种思考负担能力的方式。

sentences.en: There's inflation, the price of goods and services.
sentences.zh: 首先是通货膨胀，也就是商品和服务的价格。

sentences.en: There's interest rates, the cost of borrowing, the cost of money.
sentences.zh: 其次是利率，也就是借贷成本、资金成本。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then there's income, wages, how much workers and families actually have coming in every month.
sentences.zh: 最后是收入、工资，也就是工人和家庭每个月实际进账多少。

sentences.en: When you put all three of those together, that gives us a picture of what's happening to the cost of living, to affordability for the typical American family.
sentences.zh: 当你把这三者结合在一起时，就能让我们了解到典型美国家庭的生活成本和负担能力正在发生什么变化。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I think it makes sense to take those three factors kind of one at a time, starting with the first one, which I sense is the biggest and most obvious electoral issue, inflation.
sentences.zh: 我觉得把这三个因素逐一剖析很有意义，从第一个开始，我感觉这也是最大、最明显的选举议题，即通货膨胀。

sentences.en: Where do we stand right now?
sentences.zh: 我们目前处境如何？

sentences.en: Well, so let's go back just a little bit.
sentences.zh: 好的，那我们稍微回溯一点。

sentences.en: We all remember the huge spike in inflation that we got in 2021, 2022.
sentences.zh: 我们都记得2021年和2022年出现的通货膨胀巨大飙升。

sentences.en: It was a huge reason that the Democrats lost in 2024.
sentences.zh: 这是民主党人在2024年落败的一个巨大原因。

sentences.en: It was a huge part of President Trump's promise on the campaign trail, which was that he was going to get inflation under control.
sentences.zh: 这也是特朗普总统在竞选过程中的核心承诺之一，即他将把通货膨胀控制住。

sentences.en: Just remind us how bad it was, because while I remember it, I also kind of tried to block it out.
sentences.zh: 提醒一下当时到底有多糟，因为虽然我记得，但我其实也一直在试着把它屏蔽掉。

sentences.en: So inflation, as measured by the Consumer Price Index, right, hit 9 percent in 2022.
sentences.zh: 所以，按消费者价格指数衡量，通胀率在2022年达到了9%。

sentences.en: It was highest in 40 years.
sentences.zh: 这是40年来的最高点。

sentences.en: Wild.
sentences.zh: 太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But it had made some real progress.
sentences.zh: 但它也取得了一些实质性进展。

sentences.en: You know, by the time President Trump took office, it was down to around 3 percent.
sentences.zh: 你知道，到特朗普总统上任时，它已经降到了3%左右。

sentences.en: Most economists expected that progress to continue, to kind of get back towards what we think of as normal, which is like 2 percent.
sentences.zh: 大多数经济学家原本预计这种进展会持续下去，逐渐回到我们认为正常的水平，也就是大约2%。

sentences.en: Instead, Trump comes in, what's the first thing he does?
sentences.zh: 相反，特朗普上台了，他做的第一件事是什么？

sentences.en: He imposes tariffs.
sentences.zh: 他加征关税。

sentences.en: Tariffs are taxes on imported goods.
sentences.zh: 关税是对进口商品征收的税。

sentences.en: And so that adds to costs.
sentences.zh: 因此这增加了成本。

sentences.en: And we see inflation, progress kind of stalls out at around that 3 percent level.
sentences.zh: 我们看到通胀治理的进展在3%左右的水平停滞不前。

sentences.en: It doesn't get a ton worse, but it doesn't really get better either.
sentences.zh: 它没有变得更糟糕，但也没有真正变好。

sentences.en: And then we get into this year, and we sort of have this hope that, hey, tariffs are sort of maybe mostly behind us.
sentences.zh: 然后我们进入了今年，我们一度抱有这样的希望，嘿，关税可能已经大部分过去了吧。

sentences.en: And, you know, maybe we can get back to making progress on inflation.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，也许我们可以重新在控制通胀上取得进展。

sentences.en: And instead, President Trump makes the decision to go to war with Iran.
sentences.zh: 然而，特朗普总统却做出了与伊朗开战的决定。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, we see oil prices spike as the Strait of Hormuz gets shut down, as oil supplies around the world get constricted.
sentences.zh: 随着霍尔木兹海峡被封锁，随着全球石油供应收紧，我们突然看到油价飙升。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden, Americans are paying $4, $4.50 at the gas pump.
sentences.zh: 转眼之间，美国人在加油站要支付4美元、4.50美元的油价。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, diesel prices are hitting records.
sentences.zh: 转眼之间，柴油价格屡创新高。

sentences.en: And just talk about how the rise in oil prices affects prices across the board.
sentences.zh: 请谈谈油价上涨是如何影响各行各业价格的。

sentences.en: It's pretty clear how it affects gas prices at the pump, right?
sentences.zh: 它如何影响加油站的汽油价格，这一点很明显，对吧？

sentences.en: But my understanding is that this reaches far into many corners of the economy.
sentences.zh: 但据我理解，这已经深入影响到了经济的许多角落。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，没错。

sentences.en: So there's the obvious one, which is gas prices.
sentences.zh: 所以有一个显而易见的影响，那就是汽油价格。

sentences.en: Also, other energy prices, right, for any listeners who heat their homes with heating oil, those prices are up 74 percent from a year ago.
sentences.zh: 还有其他能源价格，对吧，对于任何用取暖油来给家里供暖的听众来说，这些价格比一年前上涨了74%。

sentences.en: We also see it in sort of energy-intensive sectors like airlines, right?
sentences.zh: 我们也看到它体现在航空等能源密集型行业中，对吧？

sentences.en: Airfares are way up because, of course, that's a huge cost for airlines.
sentences.zh: 机票价格大幅上涨，因为这当然是航空公司的一项巨额成本。

sentences.en: But then it filters through everything else, right?
sentences.zh: 但随后它会渗透到所有其他方面，对吧？

sentences.en: Diesel is what moves products around the world and around the country in trucks.
sentences.zh: 柴油是卡车在世界各地和国内运输货物的动力。

sentences.en: It's what powers tractors and combines that eventually lead to our food supply.
sentences.zh: 它是驱动拖拉机和联合收割机的动力，这些最终关系到我们的食品供应。

sentences.en: And so what starts as just an energy shock can filter through to everything else in the economy so that inflation in September – this is the data that we got last week – hits 3.7 percent.
sentences.zh: 因此，最初只是能源冲击，却能渗透到经济中的方方面面，以至于9月份的通胀率——这是我们上周得到的数据——达到了3.7%。

sentences.en: That's not 9 percent, right?
sentences.zh: 这不是9%，对吧？

sentences.en: It's not as bad as it was back then.
sentences.zh: 它没有当时那么糟糕。

sentences.en: But instead of making the progress that President Trump promised repeatedly on the campaign trail, we're actually going the opposite direction.
sentences.zh: 但我们没有取得特朗普总统在竞选期间一再承诺的进展，反而实际上在向相反的方向发展。

sentences.en: The problem is getting worse.
sentences.zh: 问题正在变得更加严重。

sentences.en: And then that leads directly into the second big issue here, which is interest rates, the cost of borrowing.
sentences.zh: 这就直接引出了这里的第二个重大问题，即利率，也就是借贷成本。

sentences.en: And just, again, remind us how these are connected, how one feeds into the other.
sentences.zh: 再次请提醒我们，这些是如何关联的，一个是如何传导到另一个的。

sentences.en: So the Federal Reserve is responsible for managing inflation.
sentences.zh: 因此，美联储负责管理通货膨胀。

sentences.en: The main tool that they use for that is interest rates.
sentences.zh: 他们为此使用的主要工具就是利率。

sentences.en: When inflation is a problem, they raise interest rates to try to slow down the economy, take it off the boil.
sentences.zh: 当通货膨胀成为问题时，他们就会提高利率，试图放缓经济，给经济降温。

sentences.en: When inflation eases, they tend to cut interest rates, allow the economy to grow a little bit faster.
sentences.zh: 当通胀缓解时，他们往往会降息，让经济增长得稍微快一点。

sentences.en: And it's similar here to the story that we just told about inflation.
sentences.zh: 这与我们刚才讲的通胀故事很相似。

sentences.en: Inflation had started to come down, and so the Fed started to ease off the brake pedal.
sentences.zh: 通胀开始回落，因此美联储开始松开刹车踏板。

sentences.en: They started to cut interest rates.
sentences.zh: 他们开始降息。

sentences.en: They started to make it a little bit easier for consumers and businesses to borrow money.
sentences.zh: 他们开始让消费者和企业更容易借到钱。

sentences.en: And then inflation picks up again, and then inflation picks up again, and the Fed has to stop.
sentences.zh: 然后通胀再次抬头，然后通胀再次抬头，美联储不得不叫停。

sentences.en: First, they stop cutting interest rates.
sentences.zh: 首先，他们停止降息。

sentences.en: And then in September, they raised interest rates for the first time in three years.
sentences.zh: 然后在9月份，他们三年多来首次加息。

sentences.en: And that filters through to, again, all of us who have to borrow money.
sentences.zh: 这再次传导到了我们所有需要借钱的人身上。

sentences.en: If you've got to put things on a credit card and carry a credit card balance, if you want to buy a car, if you want to borrow to put a machine in your factory, right,
sentences.zh: 如果你必须把账单记在信用卡上并背负信用卡余额，如果你想买车，如果你想借钱在工厂里安装机器，对吧，

sentences.en: all of this is easier if you have lower interest rates.
sentences.zh: 如果利率更低，所有这些都会更容易。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And critically, this shows up in housing.
sentences.zh: 至关重要的是，这在住房市场上表现了出来。

sentences.en: Let's talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈这个。

sentences.en: What is the relationship between these high interest rates and what we are seeing in the housing market, which seem to be really very high mortgage rates?
sentences.zh: 这些高利率与我们在住房市场上看到的情况之间有什么关系，那里的房贷利率似乎真的非常高？

sentences.en: So mortgage rates are really driven by the bond market, which we did a whole episode about not too long ago.
sentences.zh: 因此，房贷利率很大程度上是由债券市场驱动的，我们不久前刚刚做过一整期关于它的节目。

sentences.en: The relationship between the bond market and the Fed is complicated.
sentences.zh: 债券市场与美联储之间的关系很复杂。

sentences.en: But the shortest version is the same, right, which is that when inflation is rising, that tends to push up interest rates.
sentences.zh: 但最简短的结论是一样的，对吧，那就是当通货膨胀上升时，往往会推高利率。

sentences.en: It pushes up borrowing costs.
sentences.zh: 它推高了借贷成本。

sentences.en: And we've seen mortgage rates, which had been at these incredibly low levels, right, below 3 percent for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage back in the pandemic period,
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到房贷利率飙升至6%和7%，而在此之前，房贷利率一直处于令人难以置信的低水平，对吧，在疫情期间，30年期固定利率房贷甚至低于3%。

sentences.en: spike up to 6 and 7 percent.
sentences.zh: 飙升至6%和7%。

sentences.en: And they had finally, finally started to seem like they were turning around early this year.
sentences.zh: 而且它们终于、终于在今年早些时候开始显得有转机了。

sentences.en: And then, boom, inflation takes off again.
sentences.zh: 然后，轰的一声，通胀再次爆发。

sentences.en: Interest rates rise again.
sentences.zh: 利率再次上升。

sentences.en: And now you're looking at somewhere around 7 and 1⁄2 percent on a 30-year mortgage.
sentences.zh: 现在，30年期房贷的利率大约在7.5%左右。

sentences.en: And so for all of these people who have been waiting to buy homes, saving up for that down payment, thinking that finally when rates come down,
sentences.zh: 因此，对所有这些一直等待买房、为首付存钱、以为一旦利率下降，

sentences.en: I'll be able to jump into the housing market and finally buy that home years later than I had hoped to, right, they saw this moment of opportunity.
sentences.zh: 我就能跳进房市、比原本希望的晚了好几年终于买下那栋房子的人来说，对吧，他们曾看到这样一个绝佳的机会。

sentences.en: And now that has been sort of slammed shut in their face.
sentences.zh: 而现在，这个机会却被重重地当面关上了。

sentences.en: Just crushing.
sentences.zh: 简直令人心碎。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's a whole generation of people, I think, who believe that they will never be able to buy homes.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有一整代人，他们坚信自己永远买不起房。

sentences.en: And there are a lot of reasons for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后有很多原因。

sentences.en: But interest rates are clearly a huge part of it.
sentences.zh: 但利率显然是其中极重要的一部分。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Let's turn to the third factor that you flagged at the top as being crucial to the affordability picture, which is wages, people's pay,
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈你刚才指出对可负担性至关重要的第三个因素，也就是工资，大家的薪水，

sentences.en: the thing that basically determines how well or not anyone is able to handle these rising costs.
sentences.zh: 也就是从根本上决定任何人能否应对这些不断上涨的成本的关键所在。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think when we talk about affordability, right, we tend to focus on the price side of the equation.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我觉得当我们谈论可负担性时，我们往往会关注价格这一边。

sentences.en: But incomes, wages matter every bit as much, right?
sentences.zh: 但收入，也就是工资，同样至关重要，对吧？

sentences.en: If your wages are rising, you may not like rising prices, but you can manage it on some level.
sentences.zh: 如果你的工资在上涨，你或许会不喜欢物价上涨，但在某种程度上你还能应付。

sentences.en: And if you go back to that sort of post-pandemic period, we saw, you know, this period of really rapidly rising prices.
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下疫情后那段时期，你知道的，我们经历了物价飞涨的时期。

sentences.en: But we also saw rapidly rising wages.
sentences.zh: 但我们也看到了工资的迅速上涨。

sentences.en: We're in a very different environment now where wage growth has slowed significantly.
sentences.zh: 我们现在处于一个非常不同的环境中，工资增长已经大幅放缓。

sentences.en: It slowed from around 4 percent even a year ago to 3 percent today.
sentences.zh: 它从一年前的大约百分之四放缓到如今的百分之三。

sentences.en: That's not terrible on its own.
sentences.zh: 单看这一点倒不算太糟糕。

sentences.en: But if you combine that slowing wage growth from 4 percent down to 3 percent at the same moment just about that inflation has done almost the opposite, right,
sentences.zh: 但如果你把工资增长从百分之四降到百分之三，和通胀几乎完全相反的走势结合在一起，对吧，

sentences.en: gone from around 3 percent to around 4 percent.
sentences.zh: 通胀从百分之三左右升到了百分之四左右。

sentences.en: Now we have this situation where the value, the real value of people's paychecks is falling.
sentences.zh: 现在我们面临这样一种情况：人们薪水的价值，实际价值正在缩水。

sentences.en: By some measures, wages adjusted for inflation haven't grown at all since President Trump returned to office.
sentences.zh: 从某些指标来看，经过通胀调整后的工资自特朗普总统重返白宫以来根本没有增长。

sentences.en: OK, so that picture taken together sounded quite bad.
sentences.zh: 好的，这么说来，整体情况听起来相当糟糕。

sentences.en: You did say there were strengths in the economy.
sentences.zh: 但你也说过经济中存在优势。

sentences.en: Yeah, there are real strengths in the economy.
sentences.zh: 对，经济中确实存在真正的优势。

sentences.en: The challenge, I think, especially for Republicans, is that the weaknesses are really obvious and clear.
sentences.zh: 我认为，尤其是对共和党人而言，挑战在于劣势实在太明显、太清晰了。

sentences.en: They're easy to put on a campaign sign.
sentences.zh: 它们很容易被写进竞选标语里。

sentences.en: They're easy for voters to understand and to feel.
sentences.zh: 选民也很容易理解和感受到它们。

sentences.en: And the strengths are much more complicated.
sentences.zh: 而优势则要复杂得多。

sentences.en: They're nuanced.
sentences.zh: 它们更加微妙。

sentences.en: They carry caveats in a way that doesn't make for great ad copy.
sentences.zh: 它们附带各种前提条件，因此不太适合做精彩的广告文案。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnaloo.
sentences.zh: 我是温纳鲁。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏部门拼字游戏“Connections”的作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢试图捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基。

sentences.en: And I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我每天负责创作“Spelling Bee”和“Letterboxd”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特体验。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由刚才你们听到声音的这些人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 请访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: So, Ben, on to the good news.
sentences.zh: 那么，本，接下来聊聊好消息吧。

sentences.en: What are the main strengths of this economy that we're in right now?
sentences.zh: 我们目前身处的这个经济体，其主要优势是什么？

sentences.en: Well, let's start with businesses.
sentences.zh: 嗯，让我们从企业开始说起。

sentences.en: Business investment has been really strong.
sentences.zh: 企业投资非常强劲。

sentences.en: Business profits have been really strong.
sentences.zh: 企业利润非常强劲。

sentences.en: As a result of that, the stock market has been really strong.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，股市表现得非常强劲。

sentences.en: At record highs.
sentences.zh: 创下了历史新高。

sentences.en: At record after record after record.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次、不断刷新纪录。

sentences.en: So, businesses are doing well.
sentences.zh: 所以，企业目前发展势头良好。

sentences.en: They're spending on new factories and equipment to put in those factories.
sentences.zh: 它们正在斥资建设新工厂，并购买设备投入这些工厂中。

sentences.en: We're seeing a lot of new business formation, new businesses coming along.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了大量新企业的诞生和涌现。

sentences.en: But a lot of that spending is tied to AI.
sentences.zh: 但很大一部分支出都与人工智能息息相关。

sentences.en: The build out in data centers and the power plants that power them.
sentences.zh: 数据中心以及为其供电的发电厂的建设。

sentences.en: And this is where, when I said that the good news was all a little bit complicated, this is where this shows up.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么当我之前说好消息其实都有点复杂时，情况就是这样体现出来的。

sentences.en: And you started to allude to this.
sentences.zh: 你刚才也开始暗示这一点了。

sentences.en: But how should we feel about the investment being so heavily weighted towards AI?
sentences.zh: 但是，对于投资如此严重倾向于人工智能这件事，我们究竟该作何感想？

sentences.en: There's obviously been some worry about whether this AI boom potentially would turn into a bubble.
sentences.zh: 显然，一直有人担心这股人工智能热潮最终是否会演变成泡沫。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, look, the AI conversation is big and complicated.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，关于人工智能的讨论规模庞大且错综复杂。

sentences.en: And obviously, there are people who are worried about it in all sorts of different dimensions, including whether it's going to kill all of us.
sentences.zh: 显然，各方人士都在从各种不同的维度感到担忧，其中包括它是否会消灭我们所有人。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: But thinking about it from the sort of economic risk standpoint, it is this vulnerability where to the extent that we kind of have this one thing
sentences.zh: 但如果从经济风险的角度来考虑，这就成了一个脆弱点：鉴于我们把所有筹码都压在了这单一事物上，

sentences.en: that is driving everything in the economy, there's this obvious concern of what happens if the music stops.
sentences.zh: 它驱动着整个经济的一切，这里就有一个显而易见的问题：如果音乐停了会怎么样？

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we've seen some sort of subtle signs of that recently, where we've seen some of these data center companies that have kind of faltered a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们最近已经看到了一些微妙的迹象，一些数据中心公司已经出现了一点摇晃。

sentences.en: And, you know, I don't think that anybody yet is predicting a bursting of the AI bubble.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为现在还没有人预测人工智能泡沫会破裂。

sentences.en: But there is obviously this concern that if there's even a bit of a loss of enthusiasm, that could cause a pullback that would have all these ripple effects,
sentences.zh: 但显然存在这样一种担忧：哪怕热情只是稍微冷却一点，都可能导致资金回撤，从而引发一系列连锁反应，

sentences.en: that you would see fewer data centers getting built and fewer electricians getting employed to build them,
sentences.zh: 你会看到新建的数据中心减少，受雇建造它们的电工也会减少，

sentences.en: that you would see a pullback in investment, which leads to a fall in the stock market,
sentences.zh: 你会看到投资回撤，进而导致股市下跌，

sentences.en: and that potentially you could end up in a situation where the loss of enthusiasm for AI actually paves the way for a recession.
sentences.zh: 并且你最终可能会陷入这样一种境地：对人工智能热情的消退，实际上为经济衰退铺平了道路。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: We're getting dark again.
sentences.zh: 气氛又变得有些沉重了。

sentences.en: Let's get back to the strengths.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到优势上来。

sentences.en: I warned you that the strengths were complicated.
sentences.zh: 我早就警告过你，优势是很复杂的。

sentences.en: You did.
sentences.zh: 你确实说过。

sentences.en: Let me give you another complicated one, the labor market.
sentences.zh: 那我再给你讲一个复杂的优势：劳动力市场。

sentences.en: The unemployment rate is low.
sentences.zh: 失业率很低。

sentences.en: It was 4.2 percent in September.
sentences.zh: 九月份的失业率为百分之四点二。

sentences.en: It's been at or under 4.5 percent for five straight years now.
sentences.zh: 它已经连续五年保持在百分之四点五或以下了。

sentences.en: That's a record.
sentences.zh: 这是一个纪录。

sentences.en: That's a record.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是个纪录。

sentences.en: Longest ever it surpassed a period in the 1960s, right, which, again, we think of as this period of real economic strength.
sentences.zh: 这是史上最长的记录，超过了二十世纪六十年代的一段时期，对吧，而那段时期同样被我们视作经济实力真正雄厚的时期。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Like this is a legitimately good sign that says something very real about the underlying strength of the job market right now.
sentences.zh: 就像这是一个合理的积极信号，它非常真实地说明了当前就业市场潜在的强劲实力。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And yet, and yet it doesn't feel like this big, robust labor market.
sentences.zh: 然而，然而它并没有让人感觉这是一个宏大、强劲的劳动力市场。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that it's solid, but it's kind of stagnant.
sentences.zh: 原因在于它虽然稳固，但有点停滞不前。

sentences.en: You know, I think we've talked before about this low-hire, low-fire labor market.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想我们之前讨论过这种“低招聘、低解雇”的劳动力市场。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: People say this is a good time to have a job, but a bad time to be looking for one.
sentences.zh: 人们说现在是拥有一份工作的好时机，却是寻找工作的好时机。

sentences.en: They do say that, and I hate it.
sentences.zh: 人们确实这么说，而我讨厌这种说法。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Why do you hate it?
sentences.zh: 你为什么讨厌它？

sentences.en: So listen, one part of that is true.
sentences.zh: 听着，其中的一部分是对的。

sentences.en: If you are unemployed right now, it is a bad time to be looking for a job.
sentences.zh: 如果你现在失业了，这绝对不是找工作的好时机。

sentences.en: That's absolutely true.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是真的。

sentences.en: But it's not necessarily true that it's a great time to have a job.
sentences.zh: 但说现在是拥有工作的好时机，却未必完全正确。

sentences.en: I mean, listen, you would obviously rather have a job than not have a job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听着，你显然宁愿有工作也不愿失业。

sentences.en: It is better to be employed than unemployed, no question.
sentences.zh: 有工作总比失业好，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: Amen.
sentences.zh: 说得好。

sentences.en: But think about how you in your career have gone about moving up, getting wage increases, right, raising your salary.
sentences.zh: 但想想你在职业生涯中是如何一步步晋升、获得加薪的，对吧，也就是如何提高薪水的。

sentences.en: A lot of that is moving between jobs.
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是通过跳槽实现的。

sentences.en: Early in your career, you're trying to figure out what it is you want to do with your life.
sentences.zh: 在你职业生涯的早期，你还在摸索自己一生到底想做什么。

sentences.en: Later on, maybe you go and you take another great opportunity, or you threaten to take another opportunity in order to get your boss to give you a raise.
sentences.zh: 到了后来，也许你会接受另一个极好的机会，或者以此作为筹码威胁现任老板给你加薪。

sentences.en: In a moment of low hire, low fire, low turnover, there's less of that happening.
sentences.zh: 在一个低招聘、低解雇、低人员流动率的时期，这种情况就会减少。

sentences.en: And so, you know, we talked earlier about low wage growth.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如我们刚才谈到的工资增长缓慢。

sentences.en: One reason for that is that people aren't moving around between jobs.
sentences.zh: 原因之一就是人们不在不同的工作之间流动了。

sentences.en: They're not getting those raises that come with it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有获得随之而来的那些加薪。

sentences.en: And that means that it is not a labor market that is delivering consistent, strong gains for workers.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，这个劳动力市场并没有为打工人带来持续、强劲的收益。

sentences.en: And that, at the end of the day, is what people are really looking for.
sentences.zh: 而归根结底，这才是人们真正期待的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So you have explained all the complexity in the labor market.
sentences.zh: 所以你已经解释了劳动力市场的所有复杂性。

sentences.en: What else should we be looking at as a complicated strength?
sentences.zh: 我们还应该把什么看作是一种复杂的优势？

sentences.en: So if you listen to President Trump and Republicans out on the campaign trail, right, they talk a lot about strength in spending, in consumer spending.
sentences.zh: 如果你听听特朗普总统和共和党人在竞选路上的发言，对吧，他们经常谈到支出的强劲，也就是消费支出的强劲。

sentences.en: And they're right.
sentences.zh: 他们说得对。

sentences.en: We just, again, last week got retail sales data that showed that sales were up more than
sentences.zh: 我们就在刚才，就在上周获得了零售销售数据，显示销售额比去年同期增长了超过

sentences.en: 6% from a year ago, faster than expected.
sentences.zh: 百分之六，增长速度超出预期。

sentences.en: And it was just the latest piece of evidence that consumer spending has remained solid.
sentences.zh: 这恰恰是消费支出依然保持稳固的最新证据。

sentences.en: Can you just help me understand this, Ben?
sentences.zh: 能帮我理解这一点吗，本？

sentences.en: Because it just, it doesn't on its face make sense, actually, that consumer spending would be so strong, even though, as you already told us, prices have continued to go up.
sentences.zh: 因为表面上看这实在说不通，既然正如你所说物价一直在上涨，为什么消费支出还能如此强劲？

sentences.en: You are not the only one who is confused by this.
sentences.zh: 感到困惑的绝不止你一个。

sentences.en: I feel like I have been talking to economists for years now, where they keep saying, well, the consumer's got to crack eventually, and the consumer keeps not cracking.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我和经济学家们交谈了好几年，他们一直说“消费者迟早会撑不住的”，但消费者偏偏一直没有撑不住。

sentences.en: So, to some extent, I think that there is a real mystery here, and we don't fully know.
sentences.zh: 因此，在某种程度上，我认为这确实是个谜，我们尚未完全参透。

sentences.en: But I would point to two things.
sentences.zh: 但我会指出两点。

sentences.en: The first is what we were just talking about, the labor market.
sentences.zh: 首先就是我们刚才谈到的劳动力市场。

sentences.en: Yes, it's a somewhat stagnant labor market.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是一个有些停滞的劳动力市场。

sentences.en: Yes, it's not delivering great wage growth to people.
sentences.zh: 没错，它并没有给人们带来丰厚的工资增长。

sentences.en: But the fact that people do still have jobs means that most people are able to keep spending.
sentences.zh: 但人们手中仍然有工作这一事实，意味着大多数人能够继续消费。

sentences.en: We may be nervous about where things are going, but we don't have to pull back drastically, because we do still have those jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会对未来的走向感到焦虑，但我们不必大幅削减开支，因为我们确实还有那些工作。

sentences.en: And then there's this other factor, which is the stock market.
sentences.zh: 然后是另一个因素，也就是股市。

sentences.en: You know, you talked about how it's hitting records.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，你刚才提到它屡创新高。

sentences.en: Well, for people who own stock, which is most people, a majority of Americans, either on their own or in their 401k plans, own stock.
sentences.zh: 好吧，对于拥有股票的人来说，也就是大多数人，大多数美国人，无论是通过个人账户还是401k退休计划，都拥有股票。

sentences.en: But especially for the wealthiest who own most of the value of the stock market, they have seen their portfolios grow dramatically.
sentences.zh: 但尤其是对于拥有绝大部分股市财富的最富有阶层来说，他们的资产组合增长极其显著。

sentences.en: And that has given people, especially, again, the rich, the flexibility to keep spending, the confidence to keep spending.
sentences.zh: 这赋予了人们——尤其是再次强调，富裕阶层——继续消费的灵活性和继续消费的信心。

sentences.en: Ben, you know, you've been describing this sort of divide between the haves and the have-nots and how they spend.
sentences.zh: 本，你知道的，你一直在描述这种富有阶层与贫困阶层之间及其消费方式的分化。

sentences.en: There's another gap that I've kind of been thinking about just broadly as we think about the economy and how people experience it, which is a generational gap.
sentences.zh: 当我们广泛思考经济以及人们的切身体验时，我一直在思考另一个鸿沟，那就是代际鸿沟。

sentences.en: I mean, I think of all of the older folks who have already bought homes, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想到了所有那些已经买房的老年人，对吧？

sentences.en: So they're not spending on these very expensive mortgages.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不需要支付那些高昂的抵押贷款。

sentences.en: They've built up their savings.
sentences.zh: 他们已经积累了积蓄。

sentences.en: Their kids are grown.
sentences.zh: 他们的孩子已经长大成人。

sentences.en: They're not paying for child care and all of the things that cost so much in this economy.
sentences.zh: 他们不用再支付育儿费用以及在这个经济体中花费巨大的各种开销。

sentences.en: Do you see a split in generations playing out when people talk about how they feel these days?
sentences.zh: 当人们谈论近期的感受时，你是否发现代际分化正在显现？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I think that this is an economy that has so many splits in it, where one group is doing well and another group is struggling.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，我认为这是一个存在诸多撕裂的经济体，其中一个群体过得很滋润，而另一个群体在挣扎。

sentences.en: And I do think that this sort of generational divide is one of the starkest right now.
sentences.zh: 而且我确实认为这种代际鸿沟是当前最鲜明的鸿沟之一。
